text:
maria: quick UX micro-review for the routing policy editor I hacked up. current layout has a slim left rail, canvas, and a wide legend that pushes cards down on shorter screens. screenshot: https://mock.redwood/dev/rail-legend-issue.png

jon: saw it. the persistent legend is the culprit on small heights. idea: make it a fold-away strip that shows a compact row of symbols when folded and expands into the full legend on demand. keeps the canvas stable.

ashley: fold-away strip sounds promising. what about an inline mini-legend that lives above the canvas and grows into a full drawer? gives users a consistent visual anchor without stealing vertical real estate.

kevin: accessibility checklist: if legend becomes a drawer it must trap focus while open, provide `role=dialog` or `role=region` with `aria-label="Routing legend"`, and include keyboard shortcuts to open/close. ensure screen readers can toggle and read the compact state.

sam: validation point: simulation failures are currently shown as ephemeral toasts. users don't notice them. propose: 1) persistent error chip on the rule card, 2) a compact sticky banner in the left rail that lists issues and links to the offending rules. banner should survive replaying simulations until cleared.

maria: agreed. also want a clearer taxonomy: differentiate "config errors" (blocking) vs "simulation mismatches" (informational). use distinct chip styles and copy.

jon: reordering UX: drag only is rough for keyboard users. add up/down chevrons revealed on focus and support `Alt+ArrowUp/ArrowDown` for quick moves. also offer a small context menu with "Move to top/bottom" for large reorders.

ashley: the focus reveal pattern should be visually-hidden by default and exposed with `:focus-visible` so it doesn't clutter. show accessible labels like "Move rule up" for screen readers.

kevin: announcement behavior: whenever a rule is moved announce via `aria-live=polite`: "Rule \"{title}\" moved to position {n}". avoid assertive for minor UI noise. also ensure updates are debounce-controlled to avoid spamming SRs on rapid reorder.

tina: small copy change: the preview CTA currently reads "Simulate traffic" which some internal folks misinterpret. suggest "Run routing simulation" and tooltip: "Preview routing outcomes given current rules and priorities."

sam: simulation playback: we have a scrubber that autoplays results. turn autoplay off by default and provide a clear "Play" control with `aria-pressed` state and an `aria-live` region that reports the current step when playing. add markers on the timeline for notable events and a "Jump to first failure" button.

jon: when dragging rules the legend/drawer reflows and jumps around. can we freeze legend updates during drag and show a faint ghost on the map instead? less disorienting.

ashley: freezing legend is fine. alternate: throttle updates to the legend to once every 250-300ms while a drag is active. we'll prototype both and usability-test.

kevin: color/contrast nit: error chips and warning chips must meet WCAG AA at typical small sizes. our orange token fails at 12-14px. bump to deeper token or increase weight. also include high-contrast theme QA in the checklist.

maria: next steps: ashley prototype mini-legend + fold-away drawer; jon wire keyboard shortcuts + context menu; kevin write the aria announcement debounce behavior and focus trapping; sam add persistent banner + chip states and hookup to preview harness; tina will draft the updated CTA copy and tooltips. i'll iterate mocks and attach a short vid. :thumbsup:

design-bot: Task queued: "POL-UX: fold-away legend, keyboard reorder, persistent validation banner" (EPIC-3888).

jon: one more pro-tip: expose a keyboard-only reorder mode (press `r` to enter reorder, then use arrows) so power users can avoid modifier conflicts. mark it as opt-in in settings.

kevin: confirm `r` doesn't conflict with other app-wide shortcuts. map and allow remapping. add this to the keyboard shortcuts help modal.

sam: i'll add test cases for simulation mismatch vs config error and make sure the banner links anchor focus into the relevant card on click.

maria: perfect. i'll post updated screens later today and reopen the thread for quick feedback. closing for now.
